requirements.text: An effect is described by its manifest (effect.json, simai.effect.v1) alone: its identity, version, label, entry module, styles, preview, the surfaces it may be chosen for, its settings and what it needs. A product lists, describes and configures it without running its code.

Every setting has a key, a property type (choice, integer, number, boolean, string, text, color, file), a label and a valid default; numbers state their bounds, strings their longest length, choices their options, files the kinds of the site's files they accept.
A product builds the settings form from the manifest's settings with its record view; it does not hand-write a form per effect.
A product checks every stored value against its setting before saving it and before handing it to the effect; an invalid or missing value is replaced by the default, never passed on.
requirements.guidance: SF.Effects.effectSettings answers the checked settings and names the keys it dropped.

requirements.text: The entry is one module exporting mount(host, settings, context), answering update, pause, resume and destroy.
An effect draws only inside its host: it adds its own canvas or video there and touches nothing else on the page.
An effect makes no requests (needs.network is false in version 1): no fetch, no image or script from outside its own files and the site's files its settings name.
requirements.guidance: The kit fails an effect that asks for anything beyond its own files.

requirements.text: With reduced motion an effect draws one still frame and stops asking for frames; a person who turns reduced motion on is given the still frame at once.
While the tab is hidden an effect draws nothing and asks for no frames.
An effect caps its pixel density at 2.
The host is out of the accessibility tree (aria-hidden) and takes no pointer events: an effect stands under the page's controls, never over them.
New settings reach a mounted effect through update; it redraws without being mounted again.
After destroy an effect has left nothing behind -- no nodes, frames, observers or listeners -- and it can be mounted again.
An effect that fails to mount or throws is replaced by the product's default effect, and the failure is reported (sf-effect-error), never shown to the person as a broken page.

An effect not shipped and reviewed with a product runs only in an iframe sandboxed without allow-same-origin, under a strict content security policy, receiving its checked settings by message: it can never reach the page, its cookies or a form on it.
An effect is installed only after its package is checked -- the files it may hold, its size, its manifest, a digest of every file -- and installed switched off until a person turns it on.
A product runs the kit (scripts/effect-kit.mjs) on an effect before listing it: manifest, defaults, mount, no network, still motion, hidden tab, pixel ratio, update, cleanup, remount, accessibility.
requirements.guidance: The probe effect-kit runs it on a rule-keeping and a rule-breaking fixture.

uses.description: The form of effect.json: identity, entry, surfaces, typed and bounded settings, needs.

simai.ownership.scope_note: An animated background drawn into one area of a page -- a sign-in page's art side, later a hero block. The Framework owns the manifest, the module interface, the runtime rules, SF.Effects and the kit; a product owns its built-in effects, installing and turning effects on, and their settings.
